plan.english: Yesterday the father gave his own daughter to the husband, and the husband gave the bride price: four horses and a wagon. Her mother clothed her in new wool, and her sister placed a comb on her head. Then the husband led her from her house, and her two brothers walked after. Then they arrived at the husband's fence. Three times the husband led her around the Fire, and the husband's brother seated her by the Fire. The husband's brothers were looking at her, and they became astonished. Then the husband spoke: 'I am Sky; you are Earth.' Then she climbed onto the millstone. Fire, guard this wife! May sons and daughters be born to her, and may she live with the husband. May death not reach her.

Daughter, go to your husband's house! May you be mistress there. May your husband's mother and sister come to love you, and may the husband's brothers come to love you. Stand up at dawn, carry water, and make the fire ready. Work at the millstone, and may your heart not grow tired. Learn the husband's work! May you not be afraid of the husband's brothers. Your husband is a hero. Young one, do not tremble! May you see the sons of your sons, and may the gods guard you.

The young husband joined two swift horses to the wagon and drove to the young woman's house. She, wearing new wool, was standing by the wall. Her brother led her out and seated her on the wagon. Then the husband drove them away, and the husband's brothers followed her. The road was passable, and they did not go astray. A bird sat down on the fence, and it gave a sign. The husband's sister received her at the fire. The young men were drinking, and they became joyful. The husband's brothers cooked a piglet. May the gods give them good things!

Fire, giver of good things, hear us! Husband and wife, do not go apart! May you two become joyful at the dawns. Husband, protect her, and plough in the spring! Wife, follow him, and work at the millstone! May this house be filled with gifts. May it rain from the clouds, and may the fields be productive. May you two increase in wealth. May the cow-stall become full, and may the harvest season be productive. May the wolves not come near! May you two not see death.

The father spoke: 'Young man, what do you give me? My daughter knows work.' Then the young man spoke: 'I give ten cows and two swift horses as the bride price.' 'Your gifts are meager. Are you conveying gold?' 'I am conveying gold and fat.' 'Then take my daughter, and lead her away!' Then the man led her away, and she became his wife.

Daughter, you are leaving your mother. Go with your own husband! Your husband is conveying you. Daughter, put on footwear! Do not be afraid of the road! May the road be passable for you, and may the husband's brothers lead you. Wear the wool which I gave you, and remember me, and I shall remember you! May Dawn, the daughter of Sky, become bright for you, and may your heart become joyful.

title: The Wedding of the Sun's Daughter

plan.english: The daughter of the Sun was shining. Then a heavenly god arrived at the fence of the Sun, and he was seeking her. The Sun gave her to him. Her chariot was the wheel of the sun, and two swift horses were conveying her. Dawn was walking ahead, and the heavenly gods were looking at her. The Moon followed her, and the sea became bright. Then the husband received her at the fence. Gods, protect her!

Wife, enter the house! Smear fat on the wall, and sit down by the Fire! Carry the sheep and the wool inside. Do not be afraid of the husband's dog! The water is boiling. Cook the piglet! The husband's brothers are standing near, and they are looking at you. Give them gifts! May this fire burn for you. May a son be born to you, a hero, and may his name be famous.

Hero, wake up; you lie in the field. You do not listen to us, and your head has grown cold. Your swift horses are standing by the chariot. You were free, and you did not grow afraid of the serpent. You slew the serpent, and you drove the cattle to your own cow-stall. Your fame is imperishable. Your mother trembles with grief. Your wife sits in the night. Now we carry you to the Fire. Fire, convey this hero to the gods!

Lord, you are gone, and death seized you. Who now protects us? You used to give us gold and wool, and you guarded our fields. Now clouds cover the sun. The light has vanished, and your horses do not eat. Grief is in our hearts. Sleep does not come to us. We are sitting down by your wall. We remember you, and your fame is great.

Husband, you left me. The fire of your house does not burn. Your dog is seeking you, and I tremble in fear. Your sons are young. Who now leads them, and who will plough? Your harrow lies by the wall. How did you fall? You, guarding the sheep, fell at the boundary. The field is red with your blood. May men hear your good fame. I shall not marry again. Husband, I remember you.

Great lord, you lie in your own house. You who used to give us horses as gifts! You who slew the wolves, you who guarded our boundary! Now sleep grasps you. We are heating water for you, and we are stretching you out. Your brothers stand around you. The sisters sit at your head. Your chariot stands: who now drives it? May your famous name not vanish!

My son, where are you? You are lying down, and the night covers you. Your forehead has grown cold, and you were young. I nourished you, and I used to carry you around. You were growing up, and you did not become a man. Who seized you? Death seized you in the night. Mother Earth, guard him!

Let us praise this great hero. He rescued the cattle from the wolves, and he did not grow afraid of death. His heart has grown cold, and his dog lies down close by. Let us lift him, and let us lay him down. Let us place gold at his head. Let us remember his works. Hero, go on the path of the fathers! Pass by the two dogs, and may the fathers receive you.

The lord died in the night, and the birds went away. The moon did not become bright. At dawn the men carried him to the fire. The fire burned him. His wife sat down near, trembling. His dog did not eat. Then the men praised his works. They placed his name in a song. Then they built a wall around him. Lord, your name is imperishable!

Son, you were the quickest of the men. You drove the swift chariot over the boundary. A wolf was creeping in the middle of the night. You went against the wolf, and the wolf killed you. Your heart was pierced. Now your mother does not eat. She does not drink water. I, the father, carry you to the Fire. Your great fame is stretched out.

Gone is the great lord; gone is the giver of gold; gone is the master of the horses. Lord, you were our sun; you sank down; now the night has come. You gave me, the praiser, ten horses. Now who gives me gifts? Who listens to my words? I am fashioning a new song for you. It carries you to the gods.

My brother, you were a famous hero. You drove ten horses over the boundary. Then men struck you down in the night. Your blood dried on the field, and the dogs licked it. Tears fell from our mother. Our sister does not speak, and I am seeking you. I carry your name in my heart. Your good fame is imperishable.

Father Sky and Mother Earth, hear us two! We two lords have set this oath, and we two have drunk this water, and we two are joined together. I shall not drive off your horses, and you shall not drive off my sheep. Whoever breaks this oath, may thunder strike him down, and may his fields not be productive. May wolves devour him! Whoever protects this oath, may he increase in wealth!

Sky and Earth, hear me! The sun is looking at me. Moon, look at me! I am not trembling in fear. I did not take this horse, and I did not seize the master's gold. Yesterday I was sitting by my own wall. If I took it, may Earth swallow me, and may I not see the sun. If I did not take it, may my fields be productive, and may the master trust me.

title: The Warrior's Oath to His Lord

plan.english: Lord, I trust you, and I have set my oath. Sky and Earth are listening. I shall follow you, and I shall stand before you. I shall not go astray on the road. I shall guard your gifts, and I shall be alert at your fence. If I leave you, may my name vanish, and may dogs and birds devour me!

Sky and Earth, hear my words! I have taken this young woman as wife. I shall not leave her; I shall protect her, and I shall work for her, and I shall give her butter. She shall not become thirsty. I shall build a fence for her. If I strike her, may thunder strike me, and may my horses not carry me.

The man who killed the lord's son gave the lord ten piglets and three horses. Then he received the gift, and both men set an oath, and they split a sheep in two, and they drank water. The moon saw it: 'We two shall not kill again. Whoever kills again, may he be split in two!'

Our father is gone. We two brothers split his sheep in two. Now we two have set an oath, and we two shall dwell together. Sky and Earth, hear it! The moon sees us two. I shall not drive my brother's sheep into my own cow-stall. If I drive them, may death seize me, and may my fields dry up.

Men, let us set an oath! We shall not become afraid of death, and we shall go forward. Let us drink this water, and let us be alert on the road. Whoever becomes afraid, may his brothers leave him on the field. Whoever does not go astray, may he increase in wealth. Father Sky and Mother Earth, hear us, and give us swift horses!

This fat is melting in the fire. Whoever breaks this oath, may he melt! This wool is burning in the fire. Whoever breaks this oath, may his house burn! This water is boiling. Whoever breaks this oath, may his blood boil! The sun sees him, and Sky is listening to him.

I praise the lord, the giver of good things. When Dawn became bright, he gave me ten swift horses. Last year he gave eight cows. My wagon is filled with his gifts. His name is famous. I am fashioning a new song for him. I put the words in order, and they came forth.

Who gave me these four horses? The lord gave them to me as gifts. He gave three wagons; they were filled with gold. I drove them on along the road, and the men caught sight of me. I praise him, whose gifts are great. May he live, and may he not grow tired!

At the dawns the lord conveys gifts to me. Yesterday he heard my song, and his heart became joyful. Then he gave me six cows and nine sheep. He built a cow-stall for them. I am one who knows the words. He knows me, and I know him. Now my name is famous. His fame is imperishable.

Lord, giver of good things, hear the song! You gave me two chariots and four horses. You put fat before me at the dawns. The free men know you. Your horses are the quickest. Lord, may you live, and may you increase in wealth. May death not reach you!

title: New Words at the Lord's Fire

plan.english: I came to the master, and I spoke new words. Then he, sitting at the fire, was listening. Then he stood up, and he recognized me. He gave me seven cows and a horse. I drove them to my own cow-stall, and my heart became joyful. May the lord's fame be imperishable!

I am the praiser of the lord. He overcame the wolves, and he guards the boundary. He has power, and the wolves are afraid of him. He gave me five horses and wool. Men listen to my song in the night. He became famous, and I became famous. Heavenly gods, guard him!

The lord is the son of a famous father. He is awake in the night, and he protects the sheep. He gave me ten piglets and a wagon. It is carrying fat and wool. Whom shall I praise with my words? I shall praise the great lord.

The lord joined four horses to a chariot. He gave me the chariot; now I drive it. The swift dogs follow it. The men are looking at me, and I am satisfied. They are saying, 'Who gave you this chariot?' The lord, the giver of good things, gave it to me.

title: Giver of Horses, Giver of Cows

plan.english: The lord is a giver of horses; he is a giver of cows; he is a giver of gold. Who gives so many gifts? He gives so many gifts. He conveyed to me eight horses and three dogs. My heart is satisfied, and my cow-stall has become full. Men, let us praise the lord! His gifts are great.
You gave me three horses and nine sheep. In exchange I give you a song. Years go, cattle die; brothers die, gold vanishes; good fame does not die: you are in my words.

The lord cooked a piglet for me. He put cooked butter before me. Then I ate up the piglet, and I drank water. I became satisfied, and sleep came to me. He gave me two millstones and a harrow. May his house be filled with gifts! May he live!

The two brothers gave me gifts: they gave ten horses and four wagons. The horses are swift. The wagons carry wool. Their gifts are great. I praise both of them and their sisters. May their fame be stretched out!

My song, stand up, and go to the master. Speak to him at dawn: 'Your praiser is praising you. You gave him two chariots and seven piglets. He is not thirsty. Your name is famous.' Do not grow tired on the road to the master!

The gods gave wealth to the lord. He gives it to me. He gave three horses, nine cows and a cow-stall. I am fashioning a new song for him. I am his praiser. May my words become sweet to him! Fire, listen to my words! May he live!
